title: NeuroPDE: A Neuromorphic PDE Solver Based on Spintronic and Ferroelectric Devices
problem: Conventional von Neumann architecture lacks hardware-intrinsic randomness needed for efficient Monte Carlo random walk-based PDE solvers. Performance severely limited by software-based randomness generation.
motivation: Accelerate partial differential equation solving with inherent probabilistic computation capability.
method: Neuromorphic architecture leveraging emerging spintronic and ferroelectric devices: spin neurons with probabilistic transmission emulate random walks; ferroelectric synapses store continuous weights non-volatilely. Hardware-intrinsic stochasticity eliminates software randomness overhead.
key_novelty: Hardware-intrinsic probabilistic computing using spintronic devices for random walk-based PDE solving.
contributions: Spin neuron design with probabilistic transmission for random walk emulation
Ferroelectric synapse integration for non-volatile continuous weight storage
Complete neuromorphic PDE solver leveraging physical device stochasticity

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 2.7x to 29.8x energy efficiency vs CMOS neuromorphic chips

limitations: Device technology still emerging; scalability to large-scale simulations and robustness to device variations unclear.
primary_theme: neuromorphic PDE solving with emerging devices
